en.title: Lexicographically Largest Strict Mountain Sequence
en.description:
Construct n integers in the range [lo,hi] that first strictly increase and then strictly decrease; the peak is not at either end, and each phase has at least one adjacent edge. Find the lexicographically largest such sequence; output −1 if there is no solution. The original example 10,11,10,9,8, rather than the all-decreasing 11,10,..., supports forbidding an empty rising phase.

The input/output format was compiled by this site.
en.input: One line with n lo hi. The original text gives no numeric bounds; on this site 1≤n≤200000, 1≤lo≤hi≤10⁹.
en.output: If there is no solution, output only −1; otherwise, first output n, then output the n elements of the sequence.
en.explanation: The results are no solution, [10,11,10,9,8], and [9,10,9,8,7,6], respectively.
hints: Let d=hi−lo+1. At least 3 positions are needed, and at most 2d−1. To make the first item as large as possible, use the shortest feasible rising phase: the number of rising edges is p=max(1,n−d); start at hi−p, increase one by one up to hi, then decrease one by one.
